status: source correction built; not published or deployed
correctedBehavior: A valid published Entity operation may omit permissionCode in its runtime descriptor and authorization profile.
Omission is proved against current published metadata by the shared Entity authorizer. Both configured and omitted permissions use its existing scope, field-use and record-existence checks.

A declared permission still requires its exact IAM grant and catalog/binding evidence. Missing operation, malformed permission value, broken declared permission reference, unsupported runtime, and required unavailable policy remain denials.
Native lowering and publication projection compile an omitted permission without inventing a catalog permission or projection row; scope and runtime bindings remain published.

Read/list, mutation admission, descriptor actions and transfer admission use the common optional-permission entry point. Import mode support remains separately declared; missing additional mode permissions do not invent a grant requirement.
Explicit field permissions remain separate checks even when the enclosing operation has no permission.

Direct published Entity routes with no permission are admitted without fabricating permission-derived workspace/module membership; permission-bearing routes retain their existing module entitlement checks.
AI record discovery/read callers and document operation checks accept omitted Entity permissions while retaining their separate capability and document-service controls.
scopeLimits: Installed generic tenant-record and owner-record authorization profiles are supported. Other backends/resolvers/policy evaluators must be installed and qualified; omission does not activate an unsupported capability.
Legacy or domain capability contracts that independently mandate their own action permission are not globally weakened.
Product metadata definitions, permission catalog settings and source approvals were not changed. Country and existing workforce definitions retain their explicit permissions.

The source correction requires coordinated publication/deployment before it changes running behavior. Existing workforce permission MFA/risk settings and retired installed linkage functions remain outstanding from the previous handover.
